summary: Today’s pulse tracks US immigration judge allows cold-war era law to deport Wisconsin mosque’s president, What we know about stabbing on Flydubai flight to Israel, and Greetings from Syria, where time seems to melt as a glassmaker braves scorching temps. Across Guardian, BBC, and NPR, the strongest repeated signals are rights, federal, and immigration. In the background, Stella McCartney spotlights sea life at Paris fashion week as animal rights returns to headlines and Federal Reserve watchdog finds no criminal violations for building renovation cost overruns keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: US immigration judge allows cold-war era law to deport Wisconsin mosque’s president
headlines.description: When one track failed, Trump administration rushed immigration case of Palestine rights advocate Salah Sarsour An immigration judge has ruled that the president of Wisconsin’s largest mosque can be deported under a controversial, cold-war era law the Trump administration has sought to wield against foreign nationals who have been outspoken about Palestinian rights. Salah Sarsour, a US permanent resident for nearly three decades, was detained by US Immigration and Customs Enforcement in March. He was released after a federal judge found he had probably been detained in retaliation of his advocacy for Palestinian rights, which the federal judge said would render his detention unlawful.

headlines.description: The captain and first officer were injured, and one pilot has been arrested, officials say.

headlines.title: Stella McCartney spotlights sea life at Paris fashion week as animal rights returns to headlines
headlines.description: Designer is developing wool alternatives and for Paris wants focus to be on ‘sea life, not sea food’ with ocean-inspired clothes Stella McCartney has been talking about animal rights at fashion week for 30 years. She is usually a lone voice, but the issue is back in the headlines this season. Outcry over the physical restraining of a Peta protester at a catwalk show by Steven Kolb, the president of New York fashion week’s governing body, has put cruelty in wool production – previously considered a niche issue compared with the hot button topic of fur – on the news agenda. “There is no wool on the runway this season, and I’m proud of that,” McCartney said after her show. McCartney has been working on wool alternatives, including Brewed Protein, a fermented alternative to cashmere and wool developed in collaboration with the Japanese biotech firm Spiber, which was first used in her collections a year ago.

headlines.title: Federal Reserve watchdog finds no criminal violations for building renovation cost overruns
headlines.description: Trump criticized $2.4bn rehab amid attempts to pressure then Fed chair Jerome Powell into lowering interest rates The Federal Reserve ’s internal watchdog said on Wednesday that the agency has broadly mismanaged an expansive building renovation project but did not find any criminal violations, as alleged by Trump administration prosecutors. The Fed’s inspector general said that a variety of missteps by its board of governors inflated the cost of the $2.4bn renovation. The board did not secure a comprehensive cost estimate at the beginning of the project, nor did it nail down a maximum overall cost, a step that could have forced the building contractor to absorb the impact of inflation, the IG said in a 120-page report. Prices spiked after construction began in 2022.

headlines.title: Senate Democrats block datacenter energy bill
headlines.description: Republicans supported legislation although Democrats said it wouldn’t effectively address energy consumption Senate Democrats on Wednesday blocked legislation intended to offset the impact of datacenters on consumer electricity bills, which has emerged as a top voter concern ahead of November’s midterm elections . The Ratepayer Protection Act failed by a 57 to 43 vote, falling just shy of the 60-vote margin needed to advance through the Republican-controlled chamber. The House of Representatives had approved the bill by an almost unanimous vote earlier this month September.

headlinePool.title: ‘Whoever is hearing me, we need help’: how flight 1073 survived its 5,000-metre plunge
headlinePool.description: On morning service from Dubai to Tel Aviv, 150 passengers witnessed a horrific cockpit assault, flight plummet and daring rescue Pilot who stabbed co-pilot on Israel-bound plane may have tried to crash it, says Netanyahu As flight FZ 1073 soared west over the waters of the Gulf towards Israel, its passengers may have bemoaned a 20-minute delay at takeoff. For a low-cost airline route, flydubai’s daily service to Tel Aviv is usually convenient and reliable. The nonstop flight takes about three and a half hours, and departs early enough from Dubai that it usually lands at Ben Gurion airport at about 9am local time.

headlinePool.title: Grenfell fire police investigators hand files on 20 firms and 54 people to CPS
headlinePool.description: Met calls move ‘milestone’ moment that paves way for ‘very best possible evidence for charging decisions’ Police investigating the Grenfell Tower fire have asked prosecutors to consider charges including manslaughter and fraud against a range of companies and individuals. The Metropolitan police announced it had given prosecutors evidence relating to 20 companies and organisations and 54 individuals, ahead of charging decisions, in what the force described as a “milestone moment”.

headlinePool.title: Police questioning can shape a sexual assault case. Their approach is often wrong
headlinePool.description: The Cornell lawsuit filed by a woman alleging a brutal rape raises questions on how police handle such cases. The majority of police lack adequate training on trauma-informed approaches, experts say.

headlinePool.title: Six smugglers jailed for manslaughter over worst Channel small boats disaster
headlinePool.description: Thirty-one migrants died when their boat went down in November 2021. The trial found that the guilty men were part of two smuggling networks.

headlinePool.title: UK-France 'one in, one out' migrant scheme scrapped
headlinePool.description: Some 1,500 people have been removed to France since the scheme began just over a year ago.

headlinePool.title: Crews filming in Scotland told to hire locals as industry booms
headlinePool.description: While the country’s screen sector is growing, only a fraction of production staff are Scottish themselves Scotland’s striking Ardross Castle, the oldest star of The Celebrity Traitors, which kicks off on Thursday night, is just one of the stops on the Scottish tourist board’s “screen tourism” trail. From Outlander and The Odyssey filming in the Highlands and islands, to Glasgow city centre standing in for New York and Gotham City in the latest instalments of Indiana Jones and Batman respectively, film and TV is increasingly big business in Scotland. The country’s screen sector, growing year on year , is projected to be worth £1bn to the economy by 2030. But while some have celebrated the upsides of a booming production sector, others highlight a lack of opportunities for Scottish talent and the challenges of excessive tourism in areas featured on screen.

headlinePool.title: Pilot who stabbed co-pilot on Israel-bound plane may have tried to crash it, says Netanyahu
headlinePool.description: Pilot accused of attack is being questioned by Saudi authorities, PM says, as Israeli officials investigate if incident was attempted terror attack One of the pilots of a plane flying from the UAE to Israel stabbed his co-pilot and appeared to try to crash the plane, the Israeli prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, said, as Israeli officials said they were investigating whether the incident was an attempted terror attack on Israelis. The plane was forced to make an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia after the apparent attack, with the two pilots wounded but other passengers safe, according to a statement from Prince Sultan bin Abdulaziz international airport, more commonly known as Tabuk airport.

headlinePool.title: Macron says ‘welcome back’ to Burnham suggestion UK could rejoin EU
headlinePool.description: French president, speaking alongside Spanish counterpart Pedro Sánchez, says EU bid would be good news for UK and Europeans UK politics live – latest updates The French president, Emmanuel Macron, has reacted warmly to Andy Burnham’s suggestion that the UK could rejoin the EU. “Welcome back,” the French leader said in English with a smile at a news conference in Madrid on Wednesday. Macron continued in French: “If the British want to come back and if the prime minister is moving in that direction, I think that is very good news, both for his country and for the Europeans.”

headlinePool.title: Trump officials changed forms for overseas voters amid a GOP push to restrict voting
headlinePool.description: The Pentagon made last-minute changes to forms that many overseas U.S. citizens use for absentee voting, removing a category of citizens that Republicans have been pushing to block from voting.
